content:
- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast by 1–3% for high sentiment.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes (e.g., >75% increase from prior 30d) — add 2–5% buffer to forecast.
- Overshoot in early 30d forecast when sentiment is low (sentiment < 0.3) — cap forecast at 10% below recent 18d mean.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast > 3σ above recent 18d mean, reduce by 10–15% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Lagged overreaction: if forecast is high but true outcome drops 5%+ in next 5d, adjust downward by 2–4% in next forecast.
- Horizon-specific: 30d forecasts often overestimate in low volatility periods — use 18d moving average as baseline for correction.
- Sentiment-driven bias: if sentiment > 0.6, forecast should be 1–2% below true outcome; if sentiment < 0.2, forecast should be 1–2% above.
